result:
I'd probably shift how people approach disagreement—make curiosity feel more natural than defensiveness when encountering views that clash with theirs.

So much suffering seems to compound from there: conflicts that escalate because people can't imagine the other side's reasoning as anything but malice, important information that doesn't penetrate because the messenger belongs to the "wrong" group, problems that don't get solved because collaboration feels impossible.

If people more readily thought "I wonder why they see it that way" instead of "they must be wrong/bad," a lot of other things might unblock—better policy, less polarization, more actual problem-solving.

It's not a fix-all. But it feels foundational. Most of the bigger changes I'd want probably depend on it anyway.

What would you choose?
